frames.narration: PriceCalculator has one switch with 2 branches, regular and member. It is a single file, simple and tested.
Marketing asks for a third rule. The developer adds a branch inside the same function, so both existing branches are in the code being edited, and every old test has to run again.
Six more rules arrive over the year. Each addition edits the same function again. Existing branches exposed across the six edits: 27.

The team puts a DiscountRule interface in front of the rules. Now each rule is its own class with its own tests, and the engine only calls the interface. Setup costs 5 files for the 2 rules that exist.
A new rule is a new class and a line in the registry. No existing rule is in an edited file, so only the new rule's tests are new. Six more rules cost 12 touch points, against 33 for the switch.

Another team builds a plug-in framework for the same 2 rules: factories, descriptors, a loader and a context. It is 11 files before the first new rule, and it overtakes the switch only from 7 added rules.

Then a different change arrives: every rule needs the customer's country. In the switch that is one file. In the strategy design the interface, the engine and every rule change, and in the framework even more.
Closed is relative to a kind of change. Wait for the second or third real variant before abstracting, put the seam where change keeps arriving, and accept that some changes will still edit old code.
